_about: ad4 eval set. ONE rubric for every cut; per-product ground truth lives in specs/<product>.json and is read by these judges. Hard gates are pass/fail and any fail blocks ship. Soft scores are 0-1, reported only for cuts that pass every hard gate.

rules: six pieces present in cheat-sheet order (01 character script, 02 product hero, 02 her using it, 03 demo screen, 04 CTA, end card)
hook speech starts inside the first 3.0 s
master is 1080x1920 at 25 fps, runtime inside 15-20 s
burned captions sit inside the vertical safe zone (10%-80% of height)
brand string present on the end card (our own render, checked by manifest)

groundedness.gate_holder: the eye (the author on shipped cuts, the session on every clip); the LLM judge attaches a blind description and a PASS/FAIL flag as evidence, never the verdict

calibration.set: 42 film5 scenes labelled by the eye (16 FAIL, 26 PASS), calibration.json

v4 opus blind describe then judge, 8 dec.note: caught every eye-fail but never for the eye's reason (never named the phone, the tablet or the young woman); failed all three shipped clips on frames outside the 2.5 s window the cut used

calibration.reading: the judge misses object and subject substitutions (phone for ring box, tablet for umbrella, young woman for grandmother) and false-alarms on gestalt calls the eye accepts; ~40-50% disagreement however prompted, so it is a flagger, not a gate. Confound found in v3/v4: the eye labelled the trimmed window the cut used, the judge saw the whole 5 s; the pipeline now judges the used window only (panels t0/win).
calibration.how_used: ad4_physics.py judge runs describe+flag on the used window and writes llm-flag rows; the eye reads the strip plus the description and records eye:claude (session) or eye:author (shipped cuts) verdicts; build-ad4.py honours eye rows only; each eye row records whether it agreed with the flag, so the disagreement rate per leg is reported next to cost

universal_invariants: nothing spawns or vanishes mid-shot without a plausible source or exit; objects in flight came from somewhere visible or just off frame
contact precedes motion; mechanisms are causally whole (a device does what that device does, and no body part sits inside a machine)
bodies are in possible poses and stay one body; no extra or missing limbs; facial hair, clothing and age do not change within the clip
the subject's identity and the world stay constant across the clip; a new camera angle is fine, a different person or place is not
no readable gibberish, invented words, or fake brand marks on the subject or props; incidental real signage or packaging in the background is set dressing
groundedness.pass_rule: every spec proposition and every invariant PASS, each with a citing frame index

identity.note: threshold calibrated from same-look HeyGen renders vs a different-person control; SFace cosine > 0.363 is the model's own same-identity line, we run the threshold set by calibrate.py

rules: one voice across hook, VO and CTA (voice_probe.py consensus, no outlier)
STT of the audio actually used matches the script line word for word (script_match.sh exit 0)
sync_probe.py inside its band on the hook and CTA segments
no readable text in any engine clip (gibberish lettering, fake logos, signage with words)
brand string legible on the end card (manifest: we rendered it)

questions: the product-category object named in the spec is visible in b-roll a
she is using that product in b-roll b, and it is the same woman as the hook
the demo screen shows the spec's must-show fields for this product
the CTA line is specific to this product and brand
a real company in this category would run this ad as-is (1-5, pass at 4)
a human face is on screen in the first second
the spoken line is intelligible and complete inside 3 s
the line opens a question or a claim the body must resolve
there is motion or a change in the first second (not a static frame)
hook_strength.note: proxy only; the live metric is hook rate = 3s views / impressions, see online/README.md

scoring.per_cut: mean of soft scores, reported only when all hard gates pass

_note: This rubric was written for the batch that preceded the seven shipped in shoots/. Its calibration set is evals/judge-calibration.json, 42 scenes labelled by the eye. The scripts and per-product specs it names (ad4_physics.py, build-ad4.py, calibrate.py, voice_probe.py, specs/) belong to that earlier batch and are not in this repository; the numbers in the calibration block are what those scripts produced, and tests/test_suite.py checks the set against them.
